name: Kling AI Developer Platform
tagline: Paid API for Kling text-to-video, image-to-video and image generation models
description: The developer-facing side of Kling AI (Kuaishou), where the video and image generation models are sold as an HTTP API instead of a consumer web app. This specific URL is the API pricing page: prepaid resource packages, per-generation costs by model tier, and concurrency limits per package. It is for engineers wiring generated video or stills into a product, not for designers browsing a UI kit. Access needs an account and an API key.
pricing_detail: Not readable first-hand — every klingai.com and kling.ai path returned HTTP 446 to an automated fetch. Secondary sources (July 2026) report prepaid resource packages starting at a $9.80 trial pack (100 resource units, 30-day validity, 5 concurrent tasks) up to a ~$700 Standard pack (5,000 units, 20 concurrent tasks), and per-generation costs of roughly $0.18 (Kling v1) to $1.70 (v2 / v2.1 Master) for a 5-second clip, with 10-second clips at 2x. Treat these as unverified.
agent_guidance: Reach for this only when the deliverable is generated video or stills, never for UI: it ships no components, tokens or CSS. Budget before you call it — pricing is per generation and a 1080p 10-second Master clip is orders of magnitude more expensive than a v1 draft, so prototype on the cheapest model tier and only promote to Master for final renders. Do not try to scrape klingai.com for prices at build time; the domain hard-blocks non-browser clients (HTTP 446), so pin the numbers in config and have a human refresh them.
why_it_matters: Kling is one of the few frontier video models with a real public API rather than a waitlist, so it is the practical default when a product needs generated motion rather than stock footage.
evidence: https://klingai.com/global/dev/pricing (HTTP 446), https://app.klingai.com/global/dev/pricing (446), https://app.klingai.com/global/dev/document-api/apiReference/model/videoGeneration (446), https://kling.ai/dev/pricing (446); pricing figures from web search of secondary sources only (renderful.ai, atlascloud.ai, eesel.ai)

name: Fontshare Review (Abduzeedo)
tagline: Abduzeedo's write-up of Fontshare's 100 free typefaces and its ITF licence
description: An Abduzeedo article covering Fontshare, the free type library run by Indian Type Foundry. It states the library size (roughly 100 typefaces), that most are Fontshare Originals drawn in-house at ITF, that variable weights ship for many families, and that the ITF Free Font License permits personal and commercial use across print, digital and broadcast. It also points at the Pairs section, reported as 59 curated headline/body combinations shown as real editorial layouts. Useful as a licence sanity check before you commit a font in a client project.
agent_guidance: Use this as the licence-and-provenance citation for Fontshare, not as a font source — go to fontshare.com for the actual files. It is the most reputable of the several Fontshare write-ups in this index, so cite it when you need to justify to a client that a Fontshare face is safe for commercial work. Do not fetch it at runtime: abduzeedo.com sits behind Cloudflare and returns 403 to non-browser clients.
why_it_matters: Abduzeedo is a long-running design publication, so its coverage is the closest thing to an independent editorial vouch for Fontshare's unusually permissive licence.
evidence: https://abduzeedo.com/fontshare-free-fonts-100-quality-typefaces-designers (HTTP 403 on two attempts, Cloudflare); content reconstructed from web search result snippets of that exact URL

name: Fontshare Guide (Made Good)
tagline: Long-form Fontshare guide: licence terms, 15 named faces by class, Google Fonts comparison
description: A full guide to Fontshare from Made Good Designs, published 18 March 2026. It walks the platform history, the ITF Free Font License (personal, commercial, web, app-embedding and desktop use permitted; resale and redistribution not), how to download and self-host, then names picks by class: Satoshi, General Sans, Cabinet Grotesk, Switzer and Outfit for sans; Zodiak, Erode, Sentient and Bespoke Serif for serif; Clash Display, Clash Grotesk, Boska and Gambetta for display; JetBrains Mono and Chillax for mono. It closes with a Google Fonts comparison (~100 families versus 1,500+, but higher average quality and a more contemporary feel) plus limitations and an FAQ.
agent_guidance: This is the best single shortlist in the batch when you need to pick a Fontshare face fast: it is bucketed by sans / serif / display / mono, so you can go straight from a brief like 'editorial serif' to Zodiak or Sentient without browsing the library. Pair it with the Inspotype pairings entry when you need a heading plus body combination rather than one face. Watch the Google Fonts comparison numbers — they are the author's estimate, so do not quote them as fact.
why_it_matters: It converts a 100-family library into a fifteen-face decision list organised the way a designer actually chooses type, which is the hard part Fontshare's own site leaves to you.

name: Top 10 Fontshare Sans-Serifs
tagline: Ranked list of ten Fontshare sans-serif families with one-line use cases each
description: A listicle on the Bravemark agency blog, by co-founder Johan Steneros, ranking ten sans-serif families from Fontshare. In order: Satoshi (digital and print), Epilogue (wide Latin language coverage), Clash Display (corporate and editorial), Familjen Grotesk (headlines plus small text), Switzer (general modern use), General Sans (branding and corporate), Ranade (branding and corporate), Archivo (print and digital), Clash Grotesk (corporate identity and editorial), Plein (branding and medium-length text). Each entry carries designer credit and style count but little else — there are no specimens, comparisons or publication date.
agent_guidance: Thin content-marketing on an agency blog — treat it as a candidate list, not as guidance. The only thing to lift is the ten family names when you need sans-serif options beyond Inter; the descriptions are generic enough ('corporate and editorial') that they will not settle a real type decision. Prefer the Made Good Designs guide in this index, which covers the same ground with serif, display and mono picks and an explicit licence section.
why_it_matters: Marginal — it is here only because it names ten concrete Fontshare sans families in one place, which is occasionally faster than browsing the library.

name: Fontshare Pairings (Inspotype)
tagline: Eight ready heading-plus-body pairings built only from free Fontshare families
description: A pairings page from Inspotype, a typography preview platform that renders fonts and colour palettes onto real industry mockups. It presents eight heading/body combinations drawn entirely from Fontshare: Erode + Supreme, General Sans + Recia, Tanker + Bespoke Serif, Cabinet Grotesk + General Sans, Clash Display + Clash Grotesk, Gambarino + Cabinet Grotesk, Panchang + General Sans, and Excon + General Sans. Every pairing is shown with the same specimen sentence rather than a distinct use case, so the value is the combination itself, not the commentary. The parent product is free to try and claims 5,000+ designers and agencies.
pricing_detail: Free tier with a 'Try Inspotype for free' call to action; no paid tiers disclosed on this page and /pricing returns 404.
agent_guidance: This is the highest-leverage entry of the Fontshare cluster for an agent: it hands you eight pre-vetted heading/body pairs, so you can set a whole type scale in one decision instead of two. Lift the pair names straight into CSS variables and self-host the woff2 from fontshare.com — do not hotlink Inspotype. The blurbs are identical across all eight pairings, so ignore the copy and judge on the pairing structure alone (grotesk display over neutral sans, or serif body under a sans headline).
why_it_matters: Pairing is where most free-font projects fall apart, and this is a short, concrete list of combinations that are all free and commercially licensed from one foundry.
evidence: https://www.inspotype.com/blog/pairings/fontshare-fonts (fetched, all 8 pairings extracted); https://www.inspotype.com/ (fetched, returned a JS shell); https://www.inspotype.com/pricing and /blog both 404
